For the given point P(-6, 8), we have x = -6 and y = 8. Substituting these coordinate values into the origin distance formula gives: OP = sqrt((-6)^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 units. Since distance represents a physical scalar displacement, the principal square root is strictly positive, giving exactly 10 units.

questions.question: A triangle ABC is drawn to circumscribe a circle of radius 4 cm such that the segments BD and DC into which BC is divided by the point of contact D are of lengths 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. Find the lengths of sides AB and AC.

questions.question: The tangent at any point of a circle is always perpendicular to which geometric line through the point of contact?
options: The radius through the point of contact
The chord passing through the point
The line segment connecting to the opposite circumference
Any secant line drawn to the circle
questions.explanation: According to Theorem 10.1 in NCERT Mathematics, the tangent at any point of a circle is strictly perpendicular to the radius drawn through the point of contact. Proof: Let line l be the tangent touching the circle at point P with center O. Take any other point Q on line l distinct from P. Because l is a tangent, Q must lie outside the circle. Therefore, distance OQ is strictly greater than the radius OP (OQ > OP). Since this holds for every point on l other than P, OP is the shortest distance from center O to line l, proving OP is perpendicular to l.

questions.question: What is the numerical value of (sin 30 deg + cos 60 deg)?
questions.explanation: Recall the standard exact values of trigonometric ratios for special angles: sin(30°) = 1/2 and cos(60°) = 1/2. We need to evaluate: sin(30°) + cos(60°). Alternatively, using the complementary angle relationship cos(60°) = sin(90° - 60°) = sin(30°), the expression equals 2·sin(30°) = 2(1/2) = 1. (NCERT Class 10 Mathematics Chapter 8, Section 8.3).

questions.question: What is the empirical relationship between the three measures of central tendency?
questions.explanation: For moderately asymmetrical (skewed) frequency distributions, English statistician Karl Pearson established the fundamental empirical relationship connecting the three measures of central tendency: $\text{Mode} = 3\text{Median} - 2\text{Mean}$, which can also be rearranged algebraically as \text{Median} = \text{Mode} + 2\text{Mean}$ or $\text{Mean} - \text{Mode} = 3(\text{Mean} - \text{Median})$. In perfectly symmetrical distributions, all three measures coincide ($\text{Mean} = \text{Median} = \text{Mode}$), while skewness pulls the mean furthest into the long tail.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers can never represent the probability of an event?
questions.explanation: According to the fundamental axioms of probability in NCERT Class 10 Chapter 14, the probability P(E) of any empirical or theoretical event E is strictly bounded by 0 <= P(E) <= 1. Probability can never be a negative real number (such as -1.5) and can never strictly exceed 1 (or 100%). Any value outside the closed interval [0, 1] is mathematically invalid as a probability measure.

questions.question: If P(E) = 0.05, what is the probability of 'not E' (P(Ē))?
questions.explanation: The event E and its negation 'not E' (denoted as Ē) are mutually exclusive and exhaustive complementary events covering the complete sample space S. By the complementary probability theorem: P(E) + P(Ē) = 1. Given P(E) = 0.05, we compute: P(Ē) = 1 - P(E) = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95. Thus, the probability of the complementary event 'not E' occurring is precisely 0.95 (or 95%).
